caption:
बॉस! Sunny Deol की फिल्म Suryaa: Ant Se Aarambh Tak पर बड़ा कानूनी विवाद खड़ा हो गया है! 🎬

Delhi High Court में doctor Nishant Soni और अन्य डॉक्टरों ने याचिका दाखिल कर आरोप लगाया है कि फिल्म में डॉक्टरों की छवि को गलत और अपमानजनक तरीके से पेश किया गया है। डॉक्टरों का दावा है कि ऐसे गलत चित्रण से मरीजों के परिजन भड़क सकते हैं और स्वास्थ्यकर्मियों की सुरक्षा खतरे में पड़ सकती है। 🩺

वहीं मेकर्स की तरफ से सीनियर वकील Rajiv Nayar ने कोर्ट में पक्ष रखते हुए कहा कि यह फिल्म सुपरहिट मलयालम मूवी Joseph की remake है, जिसे कई राष्ट्रीय और अंतरराष्ट्रीय awards मिल चुके हैं और जिस पर कोई पाबंदी नहीं थी। ⚖️

मामले की सुनवाई करते हुए Justice Amit Mahajan की बेंच के सामने मेकर्स ने यह लिखित भरोसा दिया है कि वे trailer और मुख्य फिल्म दोनों में यह disclaimer लगाएंगे कि यह कहानी एक काल्पनिक रचना है। M. Padmakumar के निर्देशन में बनी इस फिल्म के मेकर्स के इस बयान के बाद अदालत ने याचिका को निपटा दिया है। 💥

क्या आपको लगता है कि फिल्मों में डिस्क्लेमर लगाने से विवाद सच में सुलझ जाते हैं? अपनी राय कमेंट्स में जरूर बताएं! 👇

ctx.title: Sunny Deol-starrer Suryaa to carry disclaimer in trailer and film after doctors' objection, makers tell Delhi High Court
ctx.summary: Sunny Deol-starrer Suryaa: Ant Se Aarambh Tak will include a disclaimer clarifying that it is a work of fiction and an adaptation of the Malayalam film Joseph.
ctx.text:
The Delhi High Court has recorded an undertaking from the makers of Sunny Deol -starrer Suryaa: Ant Se Aarambh Tak to include a disclaimer in the film’s trailer as well as the movie, clarifying that it is a work of fiction and an adaptation of the Malayalam film Joseph, after a group of practising doctors raised objections over its portrayal of medical professionals.
Justice Amit Mahajan, while hearing a petition filed by doctor Nishant Soni and other doctors, noted the undertaking given on behalf of the film’s producer and observed that no further orders were required to be passed in the matter.
The petitioners had approached the court apprehending that the trailer of the film projected doctors in a defamatory manner and could create an adverse perception about the medical profession.
They contended that such an incorrect portrayal of doctors could further aggravate the situation faced by frontline healthcare workers, who allegedly face attacks from disgruntled family members of patients. The petitioners argued that films portraying doctors in a negative light could create an atmosphere detrimental to their safety and reputation.
The doctors also complained that their representations to the concerned authorities had not been addressed.
Appearing for the film’s producer, senior advocate Rajiv Nayar submitted that Suryaa: Ant Se Aarambh Tak, starring Sunny Deol, was a remake of the Malayalam film Joseph, which had neither been banned by any authority nor faced restrictions. He also submitted that the original film had won several national and international awards.
Nayar further informed the court that the producer was willing to include an adequate disclaimer in both the trailer and the film, stating that the movie was a work of fiction and an adaptation of the original Malayalam film Joseph.
Taking note of the submissions, the court observed that since the film was undisputedly a remake of Joseph, which had already been released without being banned by any authority, and the producer had undertaken to include the disclaimer, no further orders were required to be passed.
The court accordingly disposed of the petition in terms of the undertaking that an appropriate disclaimer would be included in the trailer as well as the film, clarifying that it was a work of fiction and an adaptation of Joseph. The film is directed by M. Padmakumar and features Sunny Deol in the lead role.
